about.text: Activia is a brand of yoghurt made by the French company Danone, fermented with the two yoghurt bacteria and its own strain of Bifidobacterium animalis.

sources.text: The first paragraph of its article, shortened.
The photograph, its author and its licence, from its page.

how.text: Activia is a fermented milk made with the two yoghurt starters plus Danone's own Bifidobacterium strain DN-173 010, which Danone developed to survive the acidity of yoghurt. Some markets' labels also list Lactococcus lactis; the trial paper names only the two starters and the bifidobacterium, so it is left out of the table. Fermentation temperature and time are not published.

At least 6 × 10⁹ cfu of the bifidobacterium and at least 1.2 × 10⁹ cfu of the yoghurt starters (as used in a children's constipation trial)
